extracted.intended_audience: researchers preparing NIH grant applications (applicants and grant writers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on addressing the NIH 'scientific premise' expectation in grant applications — specifically what to put in the Significance and Approach sections about the rigor of prior research and how the proposed project will address weaknesses. Includes examples of the kinds of flaws reviewers expect applicants to identify.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific premise (definition)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Scientific premise refers to the rigor of the prior research being cited as key support for the research question(s)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the NIH definition quoted from the Office of Extramural Research — the focus is on the rigor of prior research (both published and unpublished) that serves as the key support for the proposed project. The NIH plans to revise application instructions and review criteria to clarify this language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance — describe strengths and weaknesses in rigor of prior research
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Significance, the applicant will be asked to "describe the strengths and weaknesses in the rigor of the prior research (both published and unpublished) that serves as the key support for the proposed project."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be concrete and pointed rather than vague. Examples of weaknesses reviewers expect called out include inadequate sample sizes, poor design, bad interpretation, use of wrong parameters or reagents, or inappropriate experimental conditions (e.g., running rodent behavioral studies in the inactive part of the daily cycle). Avoid pablum statements like "more research is needed" — list specific methodological or interpretive flaws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach — describe plans to address weaknesses in prior research
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Approach, the applicant will be asked to "describe plans to address weaknesses in the rigor of the prior research that serves as the key support for the proposed project."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain clearly how the proposed studies will remedy the specific limitations you identified in the Significance section. Provide concrete methodological, design, sample-size, or analytical strategies that directly address the prior work's weaknesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and timing of the requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The revisions are planned for research and mentored career development award applications with due dates on or after January 25, 2019.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants and reviewers should watch for NIH guide notices and updated application instructions that implement this language; it applies to applicable research/mentored career awards from that date forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider reviewer composition when critiquing prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: The blog notes that study sections often include authors of the papers you cite, their academic progeny, mentors, or close collaborators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be strategic and professional when critiquing prior literature: be factual and evidence-based in describing weaknesses, recognizing that pointed criticisms may be evaluated by authors or close colleagues of those works. Frame critiques in terms of objective methodological limitations and how your approach mitigates them rather than ad hominem or inflammatory language.
